For SQL-on-FHIR ViewDefinition chunks, test parser validation, SQL generation, DuckDB execution, and official spec fixtures/examples relevant to the chunk.

When the pipeline is fully complete, set workflow to null, set exit_reason, write all handoff files, and return control to the outer spec compliance orchestrator.

issues.spec_citation: SQL-on-FHIR v2 official validator (FHIR/sql-on-fhir.js sof-js/src/validate.js): ViewDefinition.where = {type: array, items: {type: object, required:['path'], additionalProperties:false, properties:{path,description}}}; FHIR JSON rule: repeating (max=*) elements MUST be arrays
issues.evidence: parse_view_definition accepts where:'active = true' (string), where:{path:...} (single object), and where items with unknown keys (e.g. [{'path':'x','foo':1}]) at the strict parser boundary. Official validator rejects all three. fhir4ds tests test_parser.py:678,1162 and test_duckdb.py:1789 encode the string shorthand. Probe: .temp/qa/sof_vd09_skeptic_2026_08_23/probe.py (32/32 behavior checks pass on native+fallback; this is a shape-strictness divergence only)
issues.root_cause: _parse_where delegated wholly to the permissive convenience validator validate_where_conditions, which accepts str/dict/list-of-str forms and preserves unknown keys; the strict official-JSON parser boundary never enforced the official validator schema (array of objects, additionalProperties:false) for ViewDefinition.where
issues.resolution: parser.py:_parse_where now enforces official shape before delegating: where must be a JSON array, items must be objects, item keys restricted to {path, description}; typed ParseError for violations. Permissive validate_where_conditions retained for direct-dataclass/serializer boundaries. 3 tests using string-where updated; regression class TestWhereOfficialJsonShapePerSpecSofVd09Skeptic added
